result.answer:
Gujarat — source cutoff: 2026-09-23.

Prototype source review is pending; current availability and individual eligibility are not verified.

- The two‑wheelers receive a purchase incentive of Rs 10,000 per kWh of battery capacity. [S4](https://www.powermin.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/3c383a891d96404e4b137b9e1ceb9ff9.pdf#page=5)
- The incentive applies only to two‑wheelers with a battery capacity up to 2 kWh (the value shown in column 2 of Table 2). [S4](https://www.powermin.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/3c383a891d96404e4b137b9e1ceb9ff9.pdf#page=5)
- To qualify, the vehicle’s ex‑factory price must not exceed Rs 1.5 lakhs (maximum ex‑factory price column in Table 2). [S4](https://www.powermin.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/3c383a891d96404e4b137b9e1ceb9ff9.pdf#page=5)
- The policy is operative for four years, commencing 1 July 2021 (i.e., until 30 June 2025). [S1](https://www.powermin.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/3c383a891d96404e4b137b9e1ceb9ff9.pdf#page=3)
- The demand incentive can be stacked with central‑government schemes (e.g., FAME II) but a beneficiary may claim only one Gujarat‑state scheme; multiple state‑scheme claims are prohibited. [S4](https://www.powermin.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/3c383a891d96404e4b137b9e1ceb9ff9.pdf#page=5)
- The subsidy amount is capped at the maximum battery capacity shown in column 2 of Table 2, limiting the total benefit per vehicle. [S4](https://www.powermin.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/3c383a891d96404e4b137b9e1ceb9ff9.pdf#page=5)

7. SCOPE AND ELIGIBILITY

(i) The Policy shall be applicable to all classes of electric vehic les that have taken subsidy under
the Government of India’s FAME II scheme dated 8th March 2019, F. No 1(1)/2019‐AEI and
any amendments thereafter.

(ii) The incentives for setting up a charging station shall be applicable to charging stations
meeting the guidelines and standards of the Ministry of Power Circular, dated 1st October,
2019 and any amendments thereafter.
8. INCENTIVES FOR EARLY ADOPTION OF ELECTRIC VEHICLES

(i) The Demand Incentive from the State shall be over and above any subsidies that are available
from the Central Government through its promotional schemes and policies. The subsidy shall
be disbursed directly to the customer via DBT mode from the Sta te Transport Department on
authenticating the document for the purchase of the vehicle.

(ii) The incentives for all types of electric vehicles shall be based on the electric vehicle battery
capacity (i.e energy content measured in kWh). The threshold pr ice to avail the subsidy for
each vehicle segment shall be as per Government of India’s FAME II scheme dated 8th March
2019, F. No 1(1)/2019‐AEI and any amendments thereafter.

(iii) The beneficiary can opt to get one time subsidy under any one scheme of the state

Gujarat State Electric
Vehicle Policy 2021.

Government of Gujarat
Ports and Transport Department,
Resolution No.MVD-102019-840-Kh.
Sachivalaya, Gandhinagar.
Dated the 23rd June, 2021.

1. PREAMBLE

There is an imminent shift in the nature of transportation from internal combustion vehicles to
electric vehicles. The shift to electric vehicles is being driven by a need to reduce air pollution,
reduction in India’s oil import bill and to increase energy security of the country. The thrust for electric
vehicles go hand in hand with India’s efforts to expand renewable energy capacities. In addition,
Gujarat has the highest adoption of battery operated two wheelers in the country, which makes it an
ideal proposition for industries to invest in EVs.
2. OBJECTIVES

(i) To transition the state’s transportation sector towards electric mobility.

(ii) To make Gujarat a manufacturing hub for electric vehicles and ancillary equipment.

(iii) To encourage start‐ups and investment in the field of electric mobility and associated support
sectors such as data analytics and information technology.

(iv) To improve the quality of the environment by reducing air pollution.
3. TITLE

This document shall be known as the “Gujarat State Electric Vehicle Policy 2021”
4. OPERATIVE PERIOD

(i) This policy shall be valid for a period of four years commencing from 1st July 2021.
5. ABBREVIATIONS AND DEFINITIONS

(i) “Central Government” means the Government of India;

(ii) “DBT” means Direct Benefit Transfer;

(iii) “DHI” means Department of Heavy Industry, Ministry of Heavy Industry & Public Enterprises,
Government of India;

(iv) “DisCom” means Electricity Distribution Licensee;

Gujarat State Electric Vehicle Policy ‐ 2021. 1

observations.question: According to the supplied tax notifications, for electric auto rickshaws licensed to carry up to three passengers, what are the existing tax rate, rebate and effective rate, their cost basis, the electric-power qualification and the deadline after the 2026 amendment? Does this tax extension renew the 2021 purchase subsidy?

result.answer:
Gujarat — source cutoff: 2026-09-23.

Prototype source review is pending; current availability and individual eligibility are not verified.

- Existing tax rate for electric auto‑rickshaws licensed to carry up to three passengers is 2.5 % of the vehicle’s cost. [S5](https://egazette.gujarat.gov.in/ViewPdf2.aspx?docid=202504210834101619.pdf&cdbid=04b1daad51e67cccdfe90fc07bb46679&contentType=application/pdf#page=2)
- Rebate applicable to those vehicles is 1.5 % of the vehicle’s cost. [S5](https://egazette.gujarat.gov.in/ViewPdf2.aspx?docid=202504210834101619.pdf&cdbid=04b1daad51e67cccdfe90fc07bb46679&contentType=application/pdf#page=2)
- Effective tax rate after rebate is 1 % of the vehicle’s cost. [S5](https://egazette.gujarat.gov.in/ViewPdf2.aspx?docid=202504210834101619.pdf&cdbid=04b1daad51e67cccdfe90fc07bb46679&contentType=application/pdf#page=2)
- The tax applies only to vehicles powered exclusively by an electric motor whose traction energy is supplied exclusively by an installed battery. [S4](https://egazette.gujarat.gov.in/ViewPdf2.aspx?docid=202504210834101619.pdf&cdbid=04b1daad51e67cccdfe90fc07bb46679&contentType=application/pdf#page=1)
- The deadline for this tax provision, after the 2026 amendment, is 31 March 2027. [S3](https://egazette.gujarat.gov.in/ViewPdf2.aspx?docid=20260404080501091.pdf&cdbid=eea3958b560b3b4ebb6101a297608df8&contentType=application/pdf#page=5)
- The 2026 tax extension does not renew the Gujarat State Electric Vehicle Policy 2021 purchase subsidy, which was limited to a four‑year period starting 1 July 2021. [S1](https://www.powermin.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/3c383a891d96404e4b137b9e1ceb9ff9.pdf#page=3) [S2](https://egazette.gujarat.gov.in/ViewPdf2.aspx?docid=20260404080501091.pdf&cdbid=eea3958b560b3b4ebb6101a297608df8&contentType=application/pdf#page=4)

Sources:

- [S5: Gujarat — Gujarat motor vehicle tax notification GH/PT/2025/13, PDF page 2](https://egazette.gujarat.gov.in/ViewPdf2.aspx?docid=202504210834101619.pdf&cdbid=04b1daad51e67cccdfe90fc07bb46679&contentType=application/pdf#page=2)
- [S4: Gujarat — Gujarat motor vehicle tax notification GH/PT/2025/13, PDF page 1](https://egazette.gujarat.gov.in/ViewPdf2.aspx?docid=202504210834101619.pdf&cdbid=04b1daad51e67cccdfe90fc07bb46679&contentType=application/pdf#page=1)
- [S3: Gujarat — Gujarat motor vehicle tax extension GH/PT/2026/06, PDF page 5](https://egazette.gujarat.gov.in/ViewPdf2.aspx?docid=20260404080501091.pdf&cdbid=eea3958b560b3b4ebb6101a297608df8&contentType=application/pdf#page=5)

Gujarat State Electric
Vehicle Policy 2021.

Government of Gujarat
Ports and Transport Department,
Resolution No.MVD-102019-840-Kh.
Sachivalaya, Gandhinagar.
Dated the 23rd June, 2021.

1. PREAMBLE

There is an imminent shift in the nature of transportation from internal combustion vehicles to
electric vehicles. The shift to electric vehicles is being driven by a need to reduce air pollution,
reduction in India’s oil import bill and to increase energy security of the country. The thrust for electric
vehicles go hand in hand with India’s efforts to expand renewable energy capacities. In addition,
Gujarat has the highest adoption of battery operated two wheelers in the country, which makes it an
ideal proposition for industries to invest in EVs.
2. OBJECTIVES

(i) To transition the state’s transportation sector towards electric mobility.

(ii) To make Gujarat a manufacturing hub for electric vehicles and ancillary equipment.

(iii) To encourage start‐ups and investment in the field of electric mobility and associated support
sectors such as data analytics and information technology.

(iv) To improve the quality of the environment by reducing air pollution.
3. TITLE

This document shall be known as the “Gujarat State Electric Vehicle Policy 2021”
4. OPERATIVE PERIOD

(i) This policy shall be valid for a period of four years commencing from 1st July 2021.
5. ABBREVIATIONS AND DEFINITIONS

(i) “Central Government” means the Government of India;

(ii) “DBT” means Direct Benefit Transfer;

(iii) “DHI” means Department of Heavy Industry, Ministry of Heavy Industry & Public Enterprises,
Government of India;

(iv) “DisCom” means Electricity Distribution Licensee;
